item.title: Trump Asia trip live updates: Trump greets Philippines' president ahead of meeting
item.description: Trump is scheduled this week to participate in the first-ever trilateral meeting with Putin and Xi.

item.title: PM is hollowing out defence, new Reform spokesperson warns
item.description: Andy Burnham is continuing to hollow out the armed forces just as the Conservatives did before - despite all the talk from Labour about increased investment, Reform's new defence spokesperson has said.

item.title: Peltola defeats Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, expanding Democratic majority
item.description: Democrat Mary Peltola defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in Alaska on Tuesday, completing a political comeback in a state Donald Trump has repeatedly won by wide margins. Her victory gives Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority, marking their biggest net gain in Senate seats since 1958.

item.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race: AP projects
item.description: Peltola's victory is the ninth Senate pickup for Democrats.

item.title: Mary Peltola flips Alaska's Senate seat into Democrats' column
item.description: Former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola has narrowly won Alaska's U.S. Senate race, toppling the Republican incumbent, according to a race call by The Associated Press.

item.title: Xi Jinping calls for global cooperation on AI and free trade at APEC summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping called on Wednesday for stronger global cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade, as he opened the APEC summit in Shenzhen ahead of an expected meeting with US President Donald Trump. Trade tensions and new US chip export restrictions are set to feature prominently.

item.title: National intelligence director says no signs of cyberattack amid tech outage concerns
item.description: Jay Clayton's comments come after an internal communications system used by NSA employees to share classified information temporarily went down on Tuesday.

item.title: Haitians rally behind Bukele as Salvadoran troops battle gangs
item.description: Thousands of Haitians took to the streets on Tuesday to urge El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele to keep fighting gangs, as his troops bolster security forces in the Caribbean nation. But experts warn that growing public support could turn to anger without a long-term plan to tackle violence and strengthen Haiti's police.

item.title: Middle East live: Kuwait, Bahrain report drone and missile attacks
item.description: Kuwait said Wednesday it was countering hostile drone attacks, while Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian strikes, as US allies in the Gulf remained on alert following an American attack on Iran's Qeshm Island. The incidents came amid a standoff over the Strait of Hormuz. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: UK food banks facing 'critically' low levels of donations
item.description: UK food banks are facing critically low levels of donations as they prepare for winter, according to a new report.

item.title: NJ sues to compel ICE facility operator to comply with subpoena in medical probe
item.description: The New Jersey AG is suing the operator of an ICE detention center for failing to comply with a subpoena issued in its probe into medical conditions at the facility.

item.title: Nvidia board rules that co-founder Jensen Huang will not return as CEO
item.description: Nvidia's board chairman ruled out bringing back co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO on Tuesday, as the chipmaker forecast stronger-than-expected quarterly sales but faced growing questions over its leadership, national security exposure and long-term strategy following his abrupt departure.

item.title: Trump picks LaNeve, Hegseth's former aide, as top Army officer
item.description: LaNeve was tapped for the job after Hegseth fired his predecessor.

item.title: WHO sounds the alarm on antimicrobial resistance threat
item.description: The spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is threatening modern medicine despite progress in combating drug-resistant bacteria, senior World Health Organization officials said Monday. WHO officials said countries had expanded efforts to tackle AMR, but warned that progress in prevention, diagnosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics remained too slow to meet global targets. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Jean Pierre Nyemazi, Acting Director of the WHO's AMR Department.

item.title: US Military jet wrecked while parked in Irish airport: Feds
item.description: Federal prosecutors charged an Irish national for allegedly breaking into a U.S. military jet that was parked at Shannon Airport in April and damaging it beyond repair.

item.title: Iran live updates: US conducts airstrikes on Qeshm Island, US military official says
item.description: President Donald Trump announced "major combat operations" against Iran on Feb. 28.

item.title: US, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles-free status as deaths mount
item.description: The US has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus has spread at the fastest rate in more than 30 years, while Mexico and Bolivia also lost their measles-elimination status. Vaccination rates have been falling against a number of diseases, in the US and globally, and measles has been spreading throughout the Americas since 2024.

item.title: Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as speaker in blow for Netanyahu
item.description: The Israeli parliament on Tuesday elected as new speaker an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace current Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Matan Kahana, a former special forces soldier, is expected as soon as Wednesday to start the process of undoing much of the agenda of Netanyahu.

item.title: AI imagery complicates Nigeria's election prep
item.description: In tonight's edition, concerns emerge that AI has been used to generate fake voting profiles ahead of Nigeria's high-stakes general election in January. Also, Nigeria's mining marshal heads underground to unearth some of the people and organizations behind the vast illegal mining industries. And a groundbreaking archaeological discovery in northern Sudan could be the ancient site of the largest church ever built in one of medieval Nubia's most important Christian sites.

item.title: William and Kate host glittering Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai
item.description: The Prince and Princess of Wales have hosted a star-studded event in Mumbai to celebrate the winners of the Earthshot Prize.

item.title: Major setbacks for Netanyahu ahead of vote to name new Knesset speaker
item.description: Since suffering heavy losses in Israel’s Oct. 27 election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party has repeatedly claimed the vote was “stolen” by Arab-led parties, possibly with foreign assistance. Those claims appear to be crumbling as he tries to cling to power, as the Israeli parliament is set to select a new speaker opposed to him. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: Jensen Huang says he'd be honoured to return to Nvidia as CEO
item.description: Jensen Huang makes his first public statement since resigning from Nvidia, saying he'd be honoured to return to his job amid support from the tech world. It comes ahead of a much anticipated earnings call this Tuesday, with analysts expecting the group to report a 90% jump in revenue to about $109 billion.

item.title: WATCH: Eagles Autism Foundation staff shine on game day
item.description: ABC News' Will Reeve visits Lincoln Financial Field to meet neurodivergent employees helping make Philadelphia Eagles game days special through the team's commitment to autism inclusion.

item.title: Senate Democrats demand briefings about FAA ground stop amid $50B budget ask
item.description: The funding would go to new air traffic control centers and other improvements.

item.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang: Targeted by the AI misinformation he helped create
item.description: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has become the target of a wave of AI-generated misinformation, in a striking twist for one of the men behind the AI revolution. From a fake audio recording supposedly featuring his wife to fabricated LinkedIn profiles, false claims linking him to the Chinese Communist Party and viral AI memes, Vedika Bahl examines how deepfakes and misinformation are turning against the former tech boss in Truth or Fake.

item.title: Iran 'playing mind games with the United States', expert says
item.description: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take "very seriously" any possible threat to Washington, following reports Iran was planning to target officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Monte Francis, Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center in Washington, says that Iran may be "playing mind games with the United States as a way perhaps of deterring President Trump from unleashing a massive new attack on Iran".

item.title: WATCH: CMA Awards unveil star-studded presenter lineup for country’s biggest night
item.description: ABC News' Hanna Battah reports the buzziest stories of the day in "GMA" Pop News.

item.title: Authorities take over Turkey's last pro-opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
item.description: Police raided the Istanbul headquarters of Sozcu TV on Tuesday, dealing another significant blow to Turkey's pro-opposition media. This is the third such seizure of pro-opposition media in just over a year. It comes amid public uproar over a multi-billion investment fund scandal that has affected the savings of nearly half a million people and piled pressure on President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AKP party ahead of elections in 2028. FRANCE 24's Jasper Mortimer reports from Ankara.

item.title: The centre cannot hold? Splintered moderates lag in French presidential race
item.description: Five months to go before the French vote in the presidential election first round to choose Emmanuel Macron’s successor. Not much of a race so far for the top two spots and the May Second runoff: there’s the far-right’s Marine Le Pen, the far-left’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon and way behind there’s the rest. Whether on social media or in the streets, their supporters rule. A radical break with the mainstream.

item.title: American soldier suspected of spying for Russia handed to US authorities
item.description: A US soldier arrested by UK counter terror police has been taken into custody by the American military.

item.title: Iran launches a third round of strikes on Bahrain, host of U.S. Navy's 5th Fleet
item.description: Iran fired drones on Tuesday at a U.S. radar facility in Bahrain, and the U.S. retaliated by firing at Iranian targets along an important shipping route.

item.title: Nvidia board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
item.description: The former Nvidia CEO said he would be "honored" to return if the board allowed. But the board says it has no intention of reinstating him.

item.title: Police in Philippines pursue three charges against Thomas Markle Sr
item.description: Filipino police are pursuing three charges against Thomas Markle Sr relating to child sexual abuse images, Sky News understands.

item.title: France: Protesters march for better salaries across the country
item.description: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. What started over two months ago as high school student protests has now morphed into a wider movement against the increasing cost of living.

item.title: 'A lot of anger and a weak government': Why are French public sector workers striking?
item.description: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. It follows more than a month of unrest and often violent protests led by students that the government has failed to quell. France 24's Marc Perelman explains.

item.title: Deutsche Bank leaks: German lender's dealings with Russian oligarchs under scrutiny
item.description: Germany's finance minister Tuesday urged "full transparency" from Deutsche Bank after international media outlets published reports based on millions of leaked documents that shine a light on questionable past business practices at the banking giant. They include ties to Russian oligarchs, the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, and Donald Trump before he became US president. France 24's Douglas Herbert takes a closer look.

item.title: Latest cost-of-living protests bring more than 140,000 onto the streets across France
item.description: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. Participation was lower compared to previous demonstrations, with 146,000 people demonstrating across the country, according to the interior ministry, compared with 575,000 for the previous unified protests. Unions put Tuesday's number at 550,000.

item.title: WATCH: National Geographic reveals its pictures of the year
item.description: The magazine's December issue showcases 25 of the most captivating and awe-inspiring images of 2026, selected by its editors.

item.title: Organisers hoping for 'joyful' demonstration as French public workers strike
item.description: France braced for another day of protests Tuesday as unions called for a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises. Hoping to avoid the violence that has marred recent protests in the country, organisers were hoping for a "joyous and festive" occasion, reports France 24's Claire Paccalin from a march in Paris.

item.title: Nvidia releases first results since Jensen Huang's resignation
item.description: Nvidia's chairman has reiterated the company does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO after he said he would be honoured to return to the role.

item.title: Shenzhen: Inside ‘China’s Silicon Valley’
item.description: When Xi Jinping hosts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin at this year's APEC summit, he'll be doing it in one of his country's most technologically advanced cities. Shenzhen is China's premier hub for cutting-edge tech – a place where robo-taxis and AI-powered drones are a normal part of the background... Its current status is the result of decades of policies aimed at opening up the once communist country to international markets and foreign investment.

item.title: Duffy asked for $50B for air traffic control after ground stop, a marked increase
item.description: The nationwide ground stop thrust funding for the FAA into the spotlight as Transportation Secretary Duffy and President Trump call for more money to fix a broken system.

item.title: The advice Biden got from Mitt Romney, and other takeaways from his memoir
item.description: Biden's memoir "Promise Me, America," which drops Tuesday, recounts his 2020 run for the presidency, his years in the White House and his tumultuous 2024 run.

item.title: Prague train crash leaves 46 people injured
item.description: Two trains have collided into each other near the main railway station in Prague, injuring 46 people.

item.title: Sen. Jack Reed says FAA needs a real plan, not just more money
item.description: Sen. Jack Reed raised concerns about FAA oversight of contractors after last week's nationwide ground stop and criticized the Trump administration's request for $50 billion in additional funding.

item.title: WATCH: SUV crashes into 2 driverless taxis
item.description: Police in Phoenix are investigating what led to a multi-vehicle crash involving two Waymos as self-driving cars expand into more cities across the U.S.

item.title: Can Google win the AI race without killing its cash cow?
item.description: In late October, Google had the worst stock day in its history as a public company. The Planet Money newsletter asks: has Google been caught in "the innovator's dilemma"?

item.title: I'm a human doctor with human intelligence. But I sure do like my AI notetaker
item.description: Has your doctor asked whether they can use artificial intelligence to take notes during an exam? It's very popular, and here's how to think through the pros and the cons of the new technology.

item.title: WATCH: Fiona the hippo gets a super-sized tummy ache
item.description: The Cincinnati Zoo shared that its most famous resident will be getting monitored around the clock after she "ingested an object that a visitor accidentally tossed into her habitat."

item.title: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip
item.description: Manila is President Trump's first stop on a three-day trip that will later take him to China for historic three-way nuclear talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

item.title: She went to college to become a social worker. Now she's joined the skilled trades
item.description: While the rise of AI continues to fuel the debate over whether college is worth the cost, apprenticeships in the skilled trades are having a moment, drawing in people of all backgrounds including college graduates.

item.title: UK sanctions eight firms building Israeli settlements in the West Bank
item.description: The UK has sanctioned eight firms building Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

item.title: Three Melbourne Cup trophies worth £500k each stolen
item.description: Police are searching for three Melbourne Cup trophies collectively worth more than £1.5m after they were stolen from a display cabinet at a racecourse in Melbourne.

item.title: WATCH: Pope Leo leaves Peru after historic 12-day South America trip
item.description: Pope Leo departed Peru on Monday concluding an emotional 12-day trip to South America as he recovers from cancer surgery. ABC News’ Melissa Adan reports.

item.description: What started as helping his sister make candles for a birthday party at age 13 has turned into a thriving business for New York City teen Christon Lennon.

item.description: Perley Provost, manager of Enterprise Rent-A-Car at Denver International Airport, shares how he kept stranded passengers calm and hydrated during Friday's widespread ground stop.

item.title: 'Everybody's shell-shocked': GOP operatives face 2028 prospects after midterm defeats
item.description: GOP sources told ABC News the party leaned on culture wars over costs and lost key Latino voters. Some doubt JD Vance is still the presumptive 2028 nominee.

item.title: Trump says he 'would not mind' if Jensen Huang is reinstated as Nvidia CEO
item.description: President Donald Trump said Monday morning that he "would not mind" if Jensen Huang was reinstated as CEO of Nvidia.

item.description: Here are the nominees for Album of the Year and Song of the Year at the 2027 Grammys.

item.description: ABC News' Chris Connelly breaks down the nominees for the 69th Grammy Awards with Raye leading the field with 11 nominations.

item.description: Authorities say a 500-foot Atlantic asphalt tanker collided into the American Heritage cruise ship on Friday, causing the ship to fall on its side and capsize in just 22 minutes.
